name: Four Hand Sixty Six
summary: A 32-card partnership trick-taking game where teams race to 66 card-points to win game points, first to 7 wins.
rules_text: Four Hand Sixty Six uses A-10-K-Q-J-9-8-7 in each suit, 32 cards. Players form two fixed partnerships. Dealer deals 8 cards each clockwise in 3-2-3 packets; the last card is exposed as trump and goes to the dealer for their hand. Elder hand leads. You must follow suit if able and must win the trick if you can. If void you must trump or overtrump an existing trump if able. Tricks are worth: Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2, plus 10 for last trick, total 130. Holding nine of trumps you may swap it for a higher trump once you have won a trick. On your lead you may close the game by turning down the trump; then no bonus for last trick and play stops when a side claims 66+. Scoring: 66-99 =1, 100-129=2, 130=3 game points. 65-65 carries 1 point to next hand. First side to 7 game points wins the match.
rating_reason: 32-card trick-taking, first to 66 points, strategic hidden hands
